item.title: Private Mission Launches to Extend Life of Out-of-Gas Communication Satellites
item.description: A private space mission has launched a satellite servicing effort designed to extend the operational life of aging communication satellites running low on fuel, potentially transforming the future of space infrastructure management.

item.title: Global Road Deaths Decline Since 1990, But Poorer Countries Continue to Face Rising Fatalities
item.description: A new study shows that road deaths have fallen worldwide since 1990, driven by safer vehicles, improved infrastructure, and stronger regulations, but fatalities continue increasing in many lower-income countries.

item.title: Micron's Record Earnings Silence AI Skeptics as Memory Demand Surges
item.description: Micron Technology reported record quarterly earnings and a stronger-than-expected outlook, driven by soaring AI-related memory demand and long-term supply agreements with major customers.

item.title: Mamdani Flexes Political Muscle as Progressive Allies Score Major Wins in New York House Primaries
item.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani strengthened his influence within the Democratic Party after three candidates he endorsed won key congressional primaries, defeating establishment-backed rivals and signaling a growing progressive shift in New York politics.

item.title: AI Companies Should Release Environmental Impact and Commit to Clean Energy, Says UN Chief
item.description: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has called on artificial intelligence companies to disclose their environmental impact and accelerate commitments to clean energy as AI-driven demand for computing power continues to grow worldwide.

item.title: Wyndham Clark Avoids Historic Collapse and Holds On to Win the U.S. Open
item.description: Wyndham Clark survived a dramatic final round and avoided a record collapse to capture the U.S. Open title, holding off a late charge to secure one of the most memorable victories in recent major championship history.

item.title: A Primer on Uranium Enrichment as Iran’s Nuclear Program Faces Renewed Scrutiny
item.description: As international attention focuses on Iran’s nuclear activities, understanding uranium enrichment has become essential to the debate over nuclear energy, weapons proliferation, and global security.

item.title: Movie Review: ‘The Death of Robin Hood’ Drains the Blood and Life Out of an Old English Legend
item.description: A dark and contemplative reimagining of the legendary outlaw, The Death of Robin Hood offers strong performances and striking visuals but struggles to inject vitality into the centuries-old tale.

item.title: In Georgia’s Capitol, Republicans’ Redistricting Session to Begin Without Maps
item.description: Georgia Republicans are set to begin a special redistricting session at the State Capitol without releasing new district maps, raising questions about legislative strategy, political priorities, and the future of congressional and state legislative boundaries.

item.title: See How Your Pay Compares to the CEOs of America’s Top Companies
item.description: Chief executives at the largest U.S. corporations continue to earn compensation packages worth tens of millions of dollars annually, creating a growing gap between executive pay and the wages of typical workers. New data allows employees to compare their earnings with those of CEOs at major American companies.

item.title: What to Know About Alpha-Gal Syndrome: The Life-Threatening Meat Allergy Triggered by Tick Bites3
item.description: Alpha-gal syndrome is a potentially life-threatening allergic condition caused by certain tick bites that can trigger severe reactions to red meat and animal-derived products, leaving many people unaware they have developed a dangerous food allergy.

item.title: Knicks Complete Record Rally From 29 Points Down, Beat Spurs 107-106 for 3-1 NBA Finals Lead
item.description: The New York Knicks staged a historic 29-point comeback to edge the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, taking a commanding 3-1 series lead and moving within one win of a championship.

item.title: How to Stay Safe While Traveling During Extreme Heat
item.description: Extreme heat can turn a vacation into a health emergency. Travelers can reduce risks by staying hydrated, planning activities carefully, and recognizing signs of heat-related illness.

item.title: Republicans Clash Over $1.8B Trump Settlement in Late-Night Senate Session
item.description: Republicans debated the scope and limits of a $1.8 billion settlement involving former President Donald Trump during a late-night Senate session, highlighting deep divisions within the party.

item.title: Shia LaBeouf Sentenced to Probation After Guilty Plea in Mardi Gras Bar Altercation Case
item.description: Actor Shia LaBeouf has been sentenced to probation after pleading guilty in connection with an altercation during Mardi Gras celebrations in New Orleans, resolving a legal case stemming from an incident involving bar patrons.

item.title: Trump Signs Executive Order Expanding National Security Reviews of Advanced AI Models
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a new executive order directing federal agencies to evaluate advanced artificial intelligence models for potential national security risks, cybersecurity threats, and foreign influence concerns.

item.title: Browns Trade Two-Time AP Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to Rams
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are reportedly sending star pass rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a blockbuster trade that includes Jared Verse and multiple draft picks, reshaping the NFL landscape ahead of the 2026 season.

item.title: Experimental Pill Promises New Hope for Deadly Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: Researchers say a new experimental pill targeting pancreatic cancer has shown encouraging early results, raising hopes for improved treatment options against one of the world’s deadliest forms of cancer.

item.title: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Engine Test at Launch Pad
item.description: A Blue Origin rocket exploded on the launch pad during a routine engine-firing test, sending flames and thick smoke into the sky while investigators began examining the cause of the incident.

item.title: Independent Bookstores Are Multiplying Despite the Belief They’re Dying Out
item.description: Independent bookstores are experiencing an unexpected revival across many regions, driven by community engagement, curated experiences, local support, and readers seeking alternatives to online retail giants.

item.title: Billionaire Tom Steyer’s Record Ad Spending Reshapes California Governor’s Race
item.description: Billionaire activist Tom Steyer shattered advertising spending records in California’s governor’s race, flooding television, digital platforms, and social media with campaign ads as rivals accused him of trying to buy political influence.

item.title: Puerto Rico Governor Declares Emergency to Combat Worsening Coastal Erosion
item.description: Puerto Rico's governor has declared a state of emergency in response to accelerating coastal erosion that threatens communities, infrastructure, beaches, and local ecosystems across the island. Officials are preparing measures to protect vulnerable coastal areas and address long-term environmental challenges.
item.author: Daniel C. Smith

item.title: Rubio Seeks to Rebuild Trust Between Washington and Delhi During First Official India Visit
item.description: US Senator Marco Rubio aimed to address growing trust concerns between Washington and New Delhi during his first official visit to India, focusing on strategic cooperation, regional security, trade relations, and diplomatic engagement between the two nations.

item.title: Republicans Split as Trump Pushes Emerging Iran War Deal
item.description: Several Republican lawmakers and conservative allies are criticizing President Donald Trump’s emerging proposal to end the Iran war, warning that the deal may weaken U.S. leverage against Tehran.

item.title: Nvidia Q1 Results Surpass Wall Street Expectations Thanks to Massive AI Chip Demand
item.description: NVIDIA Corporation reported stronger-than-expected first-quarter earnings as surging global demand for artificial intelligence chips continued to drive rapid revenue growth and investor optimism.

item.title: Rubio Heads to NATO Meeting as European Anxiety Over Trump, US Troops and Iran Intensifies
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is heading to a crucial NATO meeting amid growing European concerns over Donald Trump's reliability, planned US troop reductions in Europe, and rising geopolitical tensions linked to Iran.

item.title: Billie Jean King Earns College Degree at 82, Decades After Starting at Cal State LA
item.description: Tennis legend Billie Jean King has earned her college degree from California State University, Los Angeles at age 82, completing her education 65 years after first enrolling.

item.title: China Agrees to Boost US Beef, Poultry Trade After Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: China has agreed to significantly increase imports of U.S. agricultural products, including beef and poultry, following a high-level summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, signaling easing trade tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Stephon Castle scores 32 as Spurs rout Timberwolves to win Game 6
item.description: Stephon Castle scored 32 points to lead the San Antonio Spurs to a dominant 139-109 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves in Game 6, sealing the playoff series with an emphatic performance on both ends of the court.

item.title: Puerto Rico Lawmakers Debate New Energy Reform Plan to Stabilize Island's Power Grid
item.description: Lawmakers in Pue rto Rico are debating a new energy reform proposal aimed at stabilizing the island's fragile power grid and accelerating the transition toward renewable energy.
item.author: Daniel C. Smith

item.description: The United States has granted a key permit for an energy project aimed at supplying electricity to Puerto Rico from the Dominican Republic through an undersea power cable, according to the project's developer.
item.author: Daniel C. Smith

item.description: The office of the U.S. Director of National Intelligence conducted an internal review related to voting machines used in Puerto Rico, according to officials familiar with the matter, raising questions about election security and federal oversight.

item.description: Economic development leaders are promoting Puerto Rico as a strategic hub for nearshore manufacturing, highlighting its skilled workforce, proximity to the U.S. mainland, and growing industrial infrastructure.

item.description: Housing affordability concerns are increasing across Puerto Rico as rising property prices and limited housing supply place pressure on residents and first-time homebuyers.
